User-approved out-of-scope fix for the validate-time defect recorded as B-5a15:F-349, which blocked this story's TEST gate. Both files received the identical one-line change: the resources key was REMOVED from validate.commands[112] (npm --prefix packages/graph run check). ROOT CAUSE, measured not argued: that command runs packages/graph/scripts/verify-no-project-writes.mjs, which compares a whole-repo byte digest before and after its scan and deliberately hashes gitignored paths including .proof-or-stop/** (see its comment at :43-49, an intentional anti-regression choice). It previously declared a single SHARED git-common-dir claim, so the scheduler ran it concurrently with sibling commands 113-115 while validate committed its own metadata mid-run (commit 5d6f77dafe rewrote test-evidence.json by 2199 lines). The probe therefore observed the repository changing underneath it and reported UNEXPECTED_PROJECT_WRITE - detecting the harness it runs inside, not a real write leak. Reproduced on two consecutive full validate runs; passes standalone. WHY REMOVING THE KEY IS THE CORRECT FORM: resolveValidationResourceClaims (packages/main/src/core/validation-executor.ts:1656-1660) maps an EMPTY claim list to a single EXCLUSIVE barrier with exclusiveByDefault=true, while validate-resource-claims.test.mjs:245-247 requires any DECLARED list to be a SHARED barrier plus at least one further claim. My first attempt set access=exclusive on the single declared claim; that violated the invariant and broke validate.commands[75] and [107], so it was reverted. Both guards now pass: validate-resource-claims PASS (34 assertions) and red-b49d4-registration-derivation 0 RED / 26 GREEN. RESULT: validate reports 0 failures across all 116 commands, where it previously reported 115/116. ACCEPTED TRADEOFF, explicitly approved by the user: the probe is now an exclusive barrier for every story in this repo, so validate loses some parallelism - a throughput cost, not a correctness one, since serialization only removes foreign mutations from the measured window while leaving the graph-app writes the probe asserts about fully inside it. The RI-060 quality lane independently reviewed this change and passed it (RP-277), and all three lanes verified the material delta contains only these two files.

Records the scope-ack-before-sealing ordering discipline discovered as B-5a15:F-350, appended as item 8 of the existing 'Host DONE convergence / drift handling' section. Required by the project's standing rule that a fact living only in a finding or in private memory is not delivered - the project doc is the single source of truth someone follows to reproduce the work. The defect was mine: I ran scope_contract_acknowledge for the F-349 config paths AFTER acceptance-basis.json and pre-review-check.json had been sealed, and since both pin the scope-contract digest in their signature domain, the acknowledgement instantly invalidated them (AT_SCOPE_BINDING_MISSING and PR_ARTIFACT_TAMPERED) - the very gates it was meant to unblock. The round-2 test-coverage lane caught it and proved the consequence mechanically rather than asserting it: a fresh run of the pinned command returned 19/21 instead of 21/21, failing exactly at the two tests that emit the CHK-004:happy:2 and :3 selectors, with grep of both selector strings returning zero hits. The doc entry states the correct order (acknowledge, then seal, then earn), and records the blast radius precisely so a future host does not over-scope the repair: storyFilesHash does NOT move on a scope revision, so earned verificationEvidence receipts survive; what breaks is the two signed acceptance artifacts plus the reviewer run bindings, and pre_review_check being DEV-only forces a DEV round-trip if discovered in REVIEW. Documentation-only change to a doc this story is already required to keep in sync; no runtime, schema, or gate behavior is altered.

Out-of-scope but acceptance-blocking, fixed in place per defect-triage rule 1. git ls-files output crossed Node's 1MB execFileSync default as the repo grew (14997 tracked files / 1050604 bytes, over by 2028), so the verifier died with spawnSync git ENOBUFS at status:0 -- git succeeded and only the capture buffer overflowed. The full-suite runner is fail-fast, so this single terminal failure cancelled 36 downstream suites and blocked done_prepare, making it non-deferrable. Change is one added maxBuffer option plus an explanatory comment; no decision logic, allowlist, or acceptance input was relaxed. Verified both directions: clean run exits 0, and a planted deprecated-only file still exits 1 naming the stranded path, so the check is repaired rather than silenced. Root suite went from 22/58 with 36 cancelled to 58/58.
